results.basis: Q14 was raised for this feat and answered it in full, with a nine-point spec: the picks must reach a formula book and the book itself needs building. Points 1-5 fix the book's shape (add/list/reference-only/remove/search/capacity 100), point 6 ensures the character has one, point 7 gives the feat a builder picker offering only what the feat allows (Int-mod slots, potions of 9th level or lower — Q9's 'only what you may legally pick' points the same way), point 8 makes unpicked grants empty slots that open the option list, and point 9 makes the grant a one-time write severed from the book afterwards, which the feat's own 'they can't be changed' corroborates. The substitution clause is excluded by the lane manual's NOT-lanes ('prerequisites, access clauses, crafting requirements'), and the elixir re-typing has no destination under a reference-only book.
results.challengeDefect: Requirement 4 drops a mechanical clause that has a live destination in this app. The text's "You gain formulas to create these potions **as alchemical consumables with the elixir trait**" does not merely say the formulas exist — it re-types the products. Improbable Elixirs is an 18th-level **alchemist** class feat (core.json: traits ["alchemist"], category "class"), so every character who can take it already has Advanced Alchemy and Quick Alchemy, and the app's pool for both is built at C:/trying ai 2/pf2e codex/src/sheet/AlchemyPanel.tsx:42 as `Object.values(content.items).filter((it) => (it.traits ?? []).includes('alchemical') && (it.level ?? 0) <= alchLevel)`. A chosen potion is not alchemical, so it can never appear there — which is precisely what this clause is for. The feat's own next sentence names that surface explicitly: "you can use an alchemist's toolkit (**for Quick Alchemy**) or an alchemist's lab (for the Craft activity)". Requirement 4 nevertheless rules it out flatly ("Nothing here reaches the Advanced Alchemy prepare list or the Quick Alchemy picker"), and its stated ground does not hold: it argues there is "no per-character item copy to re-type" under a reference-only book, but the trait filter above keys on the item's traits at pick time, not on an inventory copy — no copy was ever needed. Nor is the exclusion owner-mandated: Q14 answers where the formulas *live* (a formula book) and is silent on what they *count as*; nine points about the book's shape are not a ruling that the grant reaches nothing else. The lane manual's NOT-lane for "crafting requirements" legitimately covers the reagent-for-components and toolkit/lab substitutions, but the re-typing is an identity change, not a crafting requirement, and the manual's own guidance says a clearly-mechanical clause with no lane is the most valuable thing to emit, not to dismiss. Level poses no obstacle either: the picks are capped at 9th level and the advanced-alchemy level here is 18. Secondary, and downstream of the same error: requirement 2 is tagged [dailyChoice] — a lane the manual defines as "chosen during daily preparations / on rest", satisfied by `dailyChoices`/`advancedAlchemy`/`dailyItems` — while requirements 3 and 4 correctly state the book write is a one-time build-time write that never touches the alchemy panel. The tag is on the wrong requirement.
results.challengeFix:
Keep requirements 1, 2 and 3 as written. Strike the sentence "Nothing here reaches the Advanced Alchemy prepare list or the Quick Alchemy picker: the decision named the book, not the alchemy panel" from requirement 4, and add a fifth requirement carrying the re-typing:

[dailyChoice] Each formula this feat writes into the book is marked, for this character, as an ALCHEMICAL CONSUMABLE WITH THE ELIXIR TRAIT — that re-typing is the load-bearing half of "You gain formulas to create these potions as alchemical consumables with the elixir trait". The consequence is a pool membership, not an inventory copy: the chosen potions must appear in the Advanced Alchemy prepare list and the Quick Alchemy picker, which select on `traits.includes('alchemical')` and a level ceiling (AlchemyPanel.tsx:42) and would otherwise never show a potion. They must likewise read as elixirs to anything keyed on the elixir trait. This is the only clause the feat has that changes what the character can make, and the feat itself names Quick Alchemy as one of the two ways these get made.

Move the [dailyChoice] tag to this new requirement — it is the one the manual's `advancedAlchemy`/`dailyItems` fields actually satisfy — and re-tag requirement 2 as the one-time build-time write it is, alongside requirement 3.

Requirement 4 then keeps only what genuinely has no lane: the reagent-for-magical-components substitution and the alchemist's-toolkit/lab permission stay as printed text, excluded by the manual's NOT-lane for crafting requirements, together with "Other than that, the formula doesn't change."
